nonblockingFindings: Ancestry receipt semantics are not stated: each ref carries only 'exit_code: 0'. Record the exact command (e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> 34a2df3b…`) in recovery-verification.json so the 'all old branch commits are already in main' claim is self-describing before the expected-SHA guarded remote deletions run.

docs/ARCHIVE.md states the bundle preserves all pre-cleanup refs 'including checkpoint refs', but the ancestry list contains only refs/heads/* and refs/remotes/origin/*; no checkpoint, stash or tag refs appear. Either add a full `git bundle list-heads` (or `for-each-ref`) receipt showing those refs, or soften the wording.

The archive tag commit is not recorded anywhere in the packet. Add the tag name -> commit (expected 34a2df3b…) and, after push, the origin tag SHA to the evidence directory; docs/ARCHIVE.md and docs/COUNCIL_REVIEWS.md GitHub links depend on that tag existing on origin before those docs are published.

The cleanup candidate commit itself is not identified by SHA. The receipts identify the recovery commit only. Record the final cleanup commit hash in the audits directory so this review can be tied to a specific tree, as COUNCIL_REVIEWS.md requires.

Manifest verification is one-directional: it confirms every manifest record matches a Git blob/size, not that every path removed by the cleanup diff appears in the manifest. A `git diff --name-status <recovery> <cleanup>` count reconciled against 1,912 records would close this.
